The test image shows a very young soybean seedling at emergence, barely out of the soil. The seedling has a green cotyledon and a brown/rotted-looking hypocotyl/root area. The soil appears wet and dark. This points to a seedling disease affecting the root/hypocotyl at emergence.

Key candidates: Pythium_damping_off (water-soaked soft rot at emergence in wet soil), Rhizoctonia (reddish-brown dry cankers at soil line), Phytophthora (chocolate-brown stem rot).

The wet soil conditions and soft-looking rot on the very young seedling strongly suggest Pythium. Let me view one reference image.

The reference image confirms the pattern - a young seedling at or near soil surface in dark wet soil showing signs of rot/collapse. The test image matches very well: a seedling at emergence with a green cotyledon but brown/rotted root-hypocotyl area, in wet dark soil. This is classic Pythium damping-off.
